summary: This bill eliminates the separate, lower minimum wage for tipped employees, requiring them to be paid the full federal minimum wage, and allows individuals to deduct qualified tips from their taxable income, subject to an income cap.

scores.thoughts: This bill introduces a new tax deduction for qualified tips, which would effectively lower the taxable income for eligible tipped employees. This directly leads to lower taxes for those individuals.

By creating a new tax deduction for tipped income, the government will collect less tax revenue. While this isn't direct spending, it represents a reduction in government funds that could be used for spending, thus indirectly impacting the government's fiscal capacity.

The bill's provision for a new tax deduction for tipped income would reduce government revenue. This reduction in revenue, without corresponding cuts in spending, could contribute to an increase in the national debt or make debt reduction more challenging.

Section 3 creates a new above-the-line deduction for qualified cash tips (with AGI cap and other limits), which reduces federal tax revenue with no offsetting revenue raisers or spending cuts. This is a core component of the bill, not a minor provision, so the legislation has a moderate deficit-increasing effect.
